dateLabel: claimed dates from c. 2600 BCE to the 1st millennium BCE (disputed)
title: Did Africa invent iron smelting independently?
place: West and Central Africa (Nigeria, Niger, Cameroon, Central African Republic)
summary: Mid-20th-century archaeologists thought ironworking reached sub-Saharan Africa from Carthage or Meroë; early radiocarbon dates from several sites have revived the case for independent invention.
why: It decides whether iron, a world-changing technology, was invented more than once.
question: Did sub-Saharan Africans invent iron smelting themselves, or did it arrive from North Africa or the Nile?
evidence: Claimed early dates include Lejja, Nigeria (2631-2458 BCE), Gbatoro, Cameroon (2368-2200 BCE) and Oboui (c. 2000 BCE); critics cite disturbed sites, old charcoal and imprecise calibration for 800-400 BCE.
wouldSettle: Securely stratified, well-dated smelting furnaces, replicated at several independent sites.

theories.name: Independent invention
theories.idea: Eggert and Holl judge local invention likely, though the evidence remains inconclusive.

theories.name: Diffusion
theories.idea: Iron came from Carthage across the Sahara or from Meroë on the Nile; Carthage now looks too late.

theories.name: Early dates unreliable
theories.idea: Clist, Killick and Alpern point to disturbed contexts and technical flaws in the early-date studies.
